clue.text: A drop of rouge in small restaurant in appropriate container

indicators.note: the A and the drop of rouge are placed inside the restaurant word

parts.note: a cafe is a small informal restaurant

indicators.note: a drop of something is a tiny bit, here just its first letter

explanation.surface: A splash of red wine served in a little bistro in a suitable vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: AR goes in after the C of CAFE. The vessel is 'appropriate' because a carafe is just what rouge (red wine) is served in.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is a glass flask used to serve wine or water, so it is a fitting container for rouge.

clue.text: Conservative has shifted support for supermarket service

indicators.note: letters that have shifted have moved into a new order

parts.note: to back someone is to support them, so back means support

explanation.surface: A Tory politician has changed his position on supporting a checkout perk.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashback is the facility at a supermarket till for drawing cash along with a purchase.

clue.text: End distribution of a drug for detachment

parts.note: the rear is the back end of something

indicators.note: distributing the letters spreads them into a new order

explanation.surface: The final stage in handing out a medicine to a military unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribution of' rearranges A DRUG into GUARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearguard is a body of troops detached to protect the back of an army, a military detachment.

clue.text: Food favourite and more rum

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for favourite in racing form
rum means odd, so more rum is odder

explanation.surface: Something to eat, a favourite drink, and extra rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' is not the spirit but the British adjective for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Fodder is food, especially dried feed for livestock.

clue.text: King inside watched criminal struck forcibly

indicators.note: the king letter goes within the rearranged word
criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are twisted

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch inside saw a villain being hit hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges WATCHED into THWACED, and 'inside' puts K between C and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To thwack is to hit with a heavy blow, so thwacked means hit hard.

clue.text: Digs private lines flanking a minister

parts.note: digs is British slang for lodgings, one's home

indicators.note: the private and lines words sit on either side of the A

parts.note: something private is secret
RY is the abbreviation for railway, lines of track

explanation.surface: A government minister's lodgings with a private telephone line.
explanation.walkthrough: SECRET and RY stand on either side of A. The Home Secretary is the UK government minister in charge of policing and immigration.
explanation.definitionFit: The Home Secretary is a senior British cabinet minister heading the Home Office.

clue.text: Racecourse trainer mostly worried about Epsom's opener

indicators.note: the shaken-up letters go around the opener of Epsom
worried suggests agitation, so the letters are shaken up
mostly means all but the last letter of trainer is used
the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A racehorse trainer is anxious about the start at Epsom racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts trainer to TRAINE, and 'worried' rearranges it into AINTRE, which goes 'about' the E of Epsom. Aintree, home of the Grand National, and Epsom are both English racecourses.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree, near Liverpool, is the racecourse that hosts the Grand National steeplechase.

clue.text: In shock, so I keeled over in booth

indicators.note: keeled over means turned upside down, so the run is read backwards
In says the letters lie within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: In a state of shock, I collapsed inside a small stall.
explanation.walkthrough: The run KSOIK sits inside 'shock so I keeled', and 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiosk is a small booth selling newspapers or tickets, or holding a telephone.

clue.text: Leave course, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the word is taken by how it is said

parts.note: a dessert is the sweet course of a meal

explanation.surface: Quit the racecourse, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' means a course of a meal, not a racecourse or a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert is to leave or abandon a place or person.

clue.text: On radio, remained composed

indicators.note: on radio means heard rather than seen, so the word is taken by its pronunciation

parts.note: remained means stayed

explanation.surface: A broadcaster stayed calm on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Staid means sober and settled in manner, close to composed.

clue.text: Ring America following very brief period of great significance

indicators.note: the ring and America letters come after the period word

parts.note: a moment is a very brief period of time
a ring is round, like the letter O
US is the abbreviation for the United States, America

explanation.surface: A ring from America after a fleeting moment matters a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentous means highly important or consequential.

clue.text: German elder in comic German opera

indicators.note: comic suggests something farcical, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An elderly German appears in a comic opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic' rearranges GERMAN ELDER IN. The definition's 'German' is the English composer Edward German, whose comic opera this is.
explanation.definitionFit: Merrie England is a 1902 English light opera by the composer Edward German.

clue.text: Having insect land on shoulder is a pet hate

indicators.note: the insect word lands on the shoulder word, coming before it

parts.note: a bug is an insect
to shoulder a burden is to bear it

explanation.surface: Having a bug alight on your shoulder is something you loathe.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear is a cause of persistent annoyance, a particular dislike.

clue.text: Attacking player in match?

definitions.meaning: a forward in football whose job is scoring goals
a match is something struck to make a flame, so it is one that strikes

explanation.definitionFit: A striker is a forward in football, and literally anything that strikes, as a match does.

clue.text: Stuff about sheep

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Fill up on a dish of mutton.
explanation.definitionFit: To cram is to stuff something full, packing it tightly.

clue.text: They can carry water from river feeding places set apart for games

indicators.note: the river letter flows into the pitches word, feeding it

parts.note: pitches are grounds marked out for games such as football
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Water from a river is piped onto the sports grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into PITCHES between E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitchers are jugs, vessels for holding and pouring water.

clue.text: Leader of 24 in commotion on trial flight

indicators.note: the leader goes within the commotion word

parts.note: a stir is a commotion
the leader of entry 24 is its first letter, an A
a case is a trial in court

explanation.surface: The head of the cabin crew causes a fuss over a test flight.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 24 is AIRCREW, so its leader is A. 'on' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is a staircase, so flight here means a set of steps.

clue.text: Female, unruly, could become perfect

parts.note: lawless means disorderly and unruly

explanation.surface: A disorderly woman might turn into a model of perfection.
explanation.definitionFit: Flawless means without any blemish, that is perfect.

clue.text: Calibre of dear item misplaced

indicators.note: misplaced letters are put in the wrong positions, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: The quality of a cherished object that has gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: The calibre of a gun or tube is its internal diameter, the width of the bore.

clue.text: Road ran out in mountainous country

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are out of place, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A road ran off into a land of mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a small principality in the Pyrenees mountains between France and Spain.

clue.text: Time and trouble taken to find private eye

parts.note: to ail is to trouble, as an illness does

explanation.surface: It takes time and effort to track down a detective.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue mirrors 22-across word for word except the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail is someone who follows a person secretly, the job of a private detective.

clue.text: Get boat repaired at home

indicators.note: something repaired is put back together, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Have the boat fixed while you stay home.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to get hold of it.

clue.text: Doctor receiving rebuke over a brandy

indicators.note: the doctor letters take in the rebuke word

parts.note: GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
a rap is a sharp rebuke

explanation.surface: A doctor who gets a telling-off over a glass of brandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappa is an Italian brandy distilled from grape pomace.

clue.text: Time and trouble taken to find retriever

parts.note: bird is slang for time served in prison
to dog is to trouble or plague persistently

explanation.surface: It takes time and effort to track down a gun dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing bird' is British slang for serving a prison sentence. The clue mirrors 19-across with a different definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird dog is a gun dog trained to find and fetch shot game birds, a retriever.

clue.text: In right state, one talking incoherently

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: In the right condition, someone speaking gibberish.
explanation.definitionFit: A raver is someone who raves, speaking wildly or deliriously.

clue.text: Regular high fliers in first class, heading for Riyadh, boasted

parts.note: A1 means first class, with the 1 read as the letter I

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: crew is an old past tense of crow, to boast

explanation.surface: Frequent flyers in first class on the way to Riyadh were bragging.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is first-class, its figure 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircrew is the crew of an aircraft, people who fly high as their regular work.

clue.text: Antagonist in graveyard's decapitated, spookily

indicators.note: spookily suggests something eerily distorted, so the letters are rearranged
decapitated means the head, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: the 's here stands for is, so it supplies an S

explanation.surface: An enemy in the cemetery has been beheaded in a ghostly way.
explanation.definitionFit: An adversary is an opponent or enemy, someone who antagonises.

clue.text: Quietly departed leaving trophy

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
the late person is one who has departed this life

explanation.surface: Someone quietly passed away, leaving a cup behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate is a trophy in the form of a silver dish, awarded in racing or sport.

clue.text: Name US conductor coming from former French province

parts.note: Eugene Ormandy was the long-serving conductor of the Philadelphia Orchestra

explanation.surface: An American maestro's name comes from an old region of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Normandy was a province of France until the provinces were abolished in 1790.

clue.text: More than one young lad, losing seconds initially, acts indecisively

indicators.note: losing means the S for seconds is taken off at the start

parts.note: a young shaver is a lad, so shavers are young lads

explanation.surface: Some young boys, losing time at the start, dither.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' says the S lost is the first letter. Havers is a Scots and northern English verb meaning to dither or talk nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To haver is to hesitate or vacillate, chiefly in Scottish usage, so havers means dithers.
